hypotheses.basis: Documented in prediction-market literature (CEPR/VoxEU analysis of 300k+ Kalshi contracts; classic parimutuel favourite-longshot bias). For THIS exchange and THIS season it is a hypothesis to be tested by the forward ledger, not an assumption.
hypotheses.statement: Favourite-longshot bias exists on Kalshi: heavy favourites (85-97c) on liquid markets are slightly under-priced, so buying them and holding to settlement earns a small positive edge after the quadratic taker fee.

hypotheses.basis: Pure forward-test hypothesis; no literature claim is asserted for Kalshi specifically.
hypotheses.statement: Expiry convergence: in the final hours before expected_expiration, 90-99c sides win often enough that 20% sizing at 90-99c is a positive-expectation trade net of fees.

hypotheses.basis: Cross-market transfer hypothesis. The source domain (equities) is NOT this market; the transfer must be proven on Kalshi's own verified prices (backtest on candles, then forward).
hypotheses.statement: 24h momentum transfers from equity/futures anomaly literature to event contracts: a 3c+ official one-day move (previous_price_dollars) predicts continuation over the holding horizon.

hypotheses.basis: Opposite of H-03. Exactly one of {H-03, H-04} should show up on a given horizon if either is real; the walk-forward split decides. Both stay in the competition so the ledger keeps both samples growing.
hypotheses.statement: Mean reversion on large moves: after a 10c+ one-day move, buying the dropped side (<=45c) reverts; equivalently the move overstates and the market corrects.

hypotheses.basis: Arithmetic consequence of the exchange's own quoting structure; the CrossHunt rule doubles as a consistency monitor — zero triggers over a season is itself a verified observation.
hypotheses.statement: Book consistency: the reciprocal quote structure (YES ask = 1 - NO bid) means a displayed pair cost YES ask + NO ask <= 0.99 should essentially never occur. When it does, it is a verified arbitrage, not a forecast.

hypotheses.basis: Microstructure transfer hypothesis (order-book imbalance is documented in equity literature). Explicitly NOT assumed to transfer; the forward ledger with full level logging is the test.
hypotheses.statement: Displayed bid-depth imbalance >= 40% predicts short-run direction on the heavier side.

hypotheses.basis: Max-return competition design: include the obvious lottery so the board shows what naive return-seeking costs. If PennyLotto ever wins, that is a research finding about longshot supply, not a fluke.
hypotheses.statement: Penny longshots (1-5c) are over-priced: the market's lottery-ticket demand makes the cheap side negative-expectation, so buying pennies is the strategy that should lose the most — tracked as the competition's deliberate failure control.

hypotheses.basis: To be verified against the committed candle archive for these series (backtest), then forward-tested. Settlement wording (rules_primary) is the risk factor and is logged per entry.
hypotheses.statement: Macro expiry closer: macro binaries (CPI/Fed) converge so fast near release that 80-97c entries inside 6h of close are positive-expectation net of fees.

hypotheses.basis: The spot-vs-strike gap argument, cross-checkable against the official settlement source named in each market's rules_primary. The market's own pricing of a physical commodity is the bridge to the cross-market DB.
hypotheses.statement: Commodity direction drift: daily price-direction binaries on established commodities sit at >=70c for one direction in the final 12h and stay there; buying that side at ask is positive-expectation.

relationships.claimed_similarity: The market should trade in expectation mode before the official release timestamp and converge violently after it; the release-to-settle window is short and the heavy side is usually right.
relationships.market_a: KXCPI (and KXFED/KXU6/KXNFP) macro binary markets on Kalshi
relationships.market_b: Official CPI / FOMC release events (BLS / Fed, official data)
relationships.transfer_test: NOT a transfer test (this is a same-market timing study): capture the release timestamp from the official source (BLS public API / Fed), capture Kalshi candles across it, measure pre/post release speed of convergence and the 80-97c hit rate inside 6h. Verdict requires BOTH committed release evidence AND committed candle evidence.
relationships.verdict_note: Blocked on: (1) fetching the official release feed into data/raw with provenance, (2) a settled KXCPI/KXFED market with candle history in the archive. Both planned; neither done in this session. Similarity to the game-markets last-mile pattern is recorded separately in R-03 and must NOT be borrowed as evidence.

relationships.claimed_similarity: Both show heavy favourites near resolution. Apparent similarity: the same 90-99c convergence shape.
relationships.market_a: Kalshi game markets (e.g. KXNFLGAME series) — last-mile favourite behaviour
relationships.market_b: Kalshi macro markets (KXCPI/KXFED) — last-mile favourite behaviour
relationships.transfer_test: Independently: run the LastMile rule on each family's OWN committed candle archive (separate data, separate verdicts). Only if both independently pass the walk-forward split does the 'shared expiry-convergence' claim get a supported label; if one fails, the relationship is coincidental at best.
relationships.verdict_note: Explicit anti-transfer discipline: the game family's result is NEVER used as evidence for the macro family, even when the price shape looks identical.

relationships.claimed_similarity: Both are two-sided bid books with visible depth; imbalance may lead price in both.
relationships.market_a: Equity microstructure (order-book imbalance -> short-run flow, documented in the equity literature)
relationships.transfer_test: Forward-only for now (Kalshi books are only captured forward): DepthDiver logs the full ladder per fill; the research DB will compute hit-rate by imbalance bucket after >= 30 verified fills. A literature claim about equities is recorded as discovery-only and is never a price or verdict source.
relationships.verdict_note: Similarity of market microstructure (bid/ask/depth) does not imply the same participants, the same order-flow composition, or the same latency structure. The ledger is the test.

relationships.claimed_similarity: The binary's 70c+ side in the final 12h should track the sign of (spot - strike) from the official source; divergence between the binary price and the spot-vs-strike gap is the measurable signal.
relationships.market_a: Kalshi daily commodity/crypto direction binaries (KXWTI/KXBTC/KXGOLD/KXETH class)
relationships.market_b: Underlying physical commodity/spot series (official settlement source named in rules_primary)
relationships.transfer_test: For each settled market: fetch the official final print (the source named in that market's rules_primary) with provenance, compare to the binary's last verified candle before settlement, and record the gap distribution. This tests whether the binary EMBODIES the physical series — a prerequisite before any cross-market strategy may treat the two as interchangeable.
relationships.verdict_note: Until this passes, CommodityDrift trades on the binary's own quote (not on the physical series), and the physical series is used only as a research cross-check.

relationships.claimed_similarity: Both quote cheap tails; the favourite-longshot bias (H-01) is claimed in the literature for Kalshi generally.
relationships.market_a: Longshot pricing on game markets (3-15c underdogs)
relationships.market_b: Longshot pricing on macro/commodity markets (3-15c tails)
relationships.transfer_test: Separate samples: LongshotFader's triggers are logged per series; after >= 20 settled fills per family, compare realised edge by family. A bias on game markets does NOT prove a bias on macro tails.
relationships.verdict_note: The literature citation (CEPR) covers the whole exchange but is third-party; per-family ledger samples are the primary evidence for this project.
